sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Radioligand binding with [3H]-PAF (0.1–500 nM) was performed 24 h post-transfection; the construct was characterized by binding assay, demonstrating the tagged receptor retains PAF-binding activity.
sites.rationale: PTAFR (UniProt P25105) has no annotated signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–16 as the sole extracellular N-terminal region, with TM1 beginning at residue 17. The paper's phrase 'immediately after the signal peptide' therefore resolves to the N-terminal extracellular face of the full-length receptor, the only extracellular terminus available for this topology-derived position. The junction is a prepend (insert_after_residue=0), placing the Flag-SNAP/Flag-Halo tag before Met-1; residue_after is confirmed as M by reading position 1 from the numbered sequence. Radioligand binding was measured and the construct was functionally characterized, supporting surface_and_function validation. Full-length human PTAFR was tagged with a double tag (Flag-SNAP or Flag-Halo) inserted immediately after the signal peptide of the full-length receptor and expressed in cells; radioligand binding with [3H]-PAF was used to characterize the construct.

literature_notes: L2 (PMID 36289206) reports mVenus, mCherry, and Rluc fused to the C-terminus of PAFR. The topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residues 297–342) firmly in the intracellular compartment; this is not a surface tag site and is recorded in other_positions. Only one extracellular surface site (N-terminal prepend) is supported by the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: mVenus, mCherry, and Rluc were fused to the intracellular C-terminus of full-length PAFR and used in functional assays; residue 342 (N) is within the intracellular C-tail (297–342) and is not accessible on the extracellular face.
